objections.claim: The macOS executable-identity recipe claims post-hash path swaps are detectable, but it specifies no operation that detects one.
objections.evidence: Lines 221-227 hash the bytes resolved by the pathname returned from proc_pidpath(T), then assert that a later path swap is detectable because T remains suspended. Suspension preserves T and its text vnode; it does not freeze the filesystem namespace. No later proc_pidpath, inode, pathname digest, or timed-launch identity check occurs before T is killed at line 257, and the later timing launches are pathname launches. Apple XNU's proc_pidpath implementation derives a string from p_textvp and then performs vnode_lookup(buf), but does not compare the looked-up vnode nvp to p_textvp (official source: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea/bsd/kern/proc_info.c#L1323-L1398). Thus keeping T suspended makes a check possible; it does not itself perform or guarantee detection. The adjacent statement that proc_pidpath(T) is P 'same inode' is likewise not operationalized against T's text vnode.
objections.proposedFix: Remove the unsupported detectability claim and explicitly make an immutable, non-concurrently-mutable digest-addressed measurement path a precondition, with path/inode/digest checks before spawn, after all target observations, and immediately before each timed launch; or name and require a concrete target-text-vnode identity comparison that binds T to the opened-and-hashed P. Any change must reject and rerun preflight. Preserve the honest statement that this remains weaker than Linux's /proc/T/exe fd hash.
